newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA SEC WANTS MORE NON-BROKERS IN BOURSE BOARD.
newsitem.headline: MANILA SEC WANTS MORE NON-BROKERS IN BOURSE BOARD.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said on Thursday it favours more non-brokers in the Philippine Stock Exchange's (PSE) board of governors to further professionalise stock market operations.
SEC chairman Perfecto Yasay said in a speech at the Philippine Futuristics Society the regulatory body wants six or seven non-brokers as governors of the stock exchange.
At present, only three out of the 15-man board of governors are non-brokers. They are businessman Washington Sycip, Petron Corp chairman Monico Jacob and PSE president Jose Yulo.

"The objective is to work towards further professionalisation of the PSE. This is not an imposition but merely an encouragement for the granting of a self-regulatory organisation (SRO) status," Yasay said.

The board of governors is the highest policy-making body of the Philippine bourse. It is divided into committees to handle activities such as listings, business conduct, initial public offerings and membership.
The inclusion of non-broker members last year was one of the requirements imposed by the SEC on the stock exchange as part of the latter's bid for a self-regulatory organisation status.
An SRO status will allow the exchange to police its own ranks, conduct investigations and impose sanctions without passing through the SEC.
